candidates.text: When the protocol uses Borrow-Lend supply values as backing, totalBackingSigned() must account for Borrow-Lend liabilities (borrow.value) rather than treating the 0x811 state as supply-only.
evidence_ids: `MonetrixAccountant` treats HyperCore 0x811 Borrow-Lend state as supply-only. It counts `supply.value` as protocol backing, but it never reads or subtracts `borrow.value`.

The bug is in the Accountant's interpretation of the 0x811 state. Once the protocol uses Borrow-Lend supply values as backing, it must also account for Borrow-Lend liabilities. The contracts do not enforce `borrow.value == 0`, do not subtract `borrow.value`, and do not prove the liability is netted elsewhere before settling yield.

That state exposes an asset side and a liability side. Treating the returned state as supply-only is economically incorrect. See [`PrecompileLib.sol`](https://github.com/hyperliquid-dev/hyper-evm-lib/blob/main/src/PrecompileLib.sol).

candidates.text: The settleDailyPnL() distributable-surplus gate must prevent settlement above real distributable surplus under net backing.
evidence_ids: Gate 3 is intended to prevent settlement above real distributable surplus. Because Borrow-Lend liabilities are omitted, this gate can approve yield that does not exist under net backing.

The Accountant is the on-chain gate that should prevent phantom surplus from being settled. The Operator submits an amount that the on-chain gate accepts. The failure is that the gate is computed from gross supply accounting instead of net Borrow-Lend accounting.

candidates.text: Yield settlement must not move real USDC into YieldEscrow as yield when net backing has no surplus.
evidence_ids: Because Monetrix only accounts the positive supply side, a Borrow-Lend liability can be omitted from backing. This inflates `totalBackingSigned()`, makes `surplus()` and `distributableSurplus()` artificially positive, and allows `MonetrixVault.settle()` to move real USDC into `YieldEscrow` as yield even when the correct net surplus is zero.
This converts the accounting error into a real asset movement. USDC leaves the Vault and enters `YieldEscrow` as yield even though net backing has no surplus.
